summary: Revision of r1 to resolve the planchecker conflict: the builder changed the requirement so BOOT-001 is proven by a start-up smoke runner, scripts/smoke/run.mjs, in addition to in-process tests. Everything else in r1 stands. The Identity work already on the branch is kept and only gaps are finished; nothing is rebuilt. Cloud mode runs ASP.NET Core Identity over a Dapper/QBuilder IUserStore (no EF Core, no new package): 7-day cookie sessions, 5-failures/5-minute lockout, Google through the framework's OAuth handler, one fixed role per person (Admin/Operator/Viewer, a single Role column exposed through an IUserRoleStore adapter plus role and company_id claims, no RoleManager or role table), and tenancy taken from the signed-in person's CompanyId claim only (never a header or subdomain). Legacy password hashes are accepted by LegacyAwarePasswordHasher and re-hashed on first successful sign-in; legacy IsAdmin maps to Admin, others to Operator so nobody loses access. Desktop/local mode registers no auth and keeps its SQLite stores, so data stays intact (R11), and is bound to loopback only. The old stack (AuthRouter, JwtMiddleware, JwtService, TokenService, SetupService, PasswordHelper, RefreshToken, ResetToken) is already deleted. NEW IN THIS ROUND: add scripts/smoke/run.mjs at the project root (plain Node, no new npm package, no databases or secrets). It picks a free loopback port and a temp SHIPRIGHT_DATA_DIR, starts the built ShipRight.Server in desktop/local mode (SHIPRIGHT_PORT, no cloud settings), polls /api/health with a bounded timeout (60s, 250ms steps), then GETs / (home page must return 200 HTML) and /api/projects (must return 200 JSON with no credentials) and checks that no sign-in route is exposed; it always kills the child process and deletes the temp dir in a finally block, prints verbose step-by-step output (per project feedback), and exits 0 on success or non-zero with the failing step. Where wwwroot/index.html is absent from the build output (MapFallbackToFile needs it), the runner stages a copy of the front-end export (front-end/out) or a minimal placeholder index.html into a temp content directory rather than touching tracked files. Its presence is what switches on the project's app-boots check (BOOT-001), so it is written test-first: a small jest or node:test check of the runner's helpers and an in-process BootInProcessTests run (desktop mode: /api/health, /, /api/projects with no credentials; cloud mode against the test MariaDB: 401 then 200 after register) back it up. Remaining work, strictly test-first: (1) run the full backend, jest and tsc suites to confirm the baseline and fix anything red; (2) close hardening gaps each with a failing test first: session cookie Secure always in cloud mode, security stamp rotated on role change, switch-off and password reset so old sessions and reset links die, Google link-on-match only when Google reports the email verified (accepted risk noted in SETUP.md), DataProtection keys under the resolved SHIPRIGHT_DATA_DIR; (3) every public endpoint (login, register, providers, forgot-password, reset-password, google start/complete) carries an AllowAnonymous reason comment, and a route-sweep test calls every endpoint without credentials and expects 401 except that list (API-001); (4) a settings-agreement test compares .env.example, docker-compose.yml and CloudConfiguration exactly (JWT key and first-admin seed removed, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET added, SMTP kept); (5) confirm tests for lockout, sign-in and a 50-person team list under 1 second, no partial company/person rows on forced failure (company and person written in one transaction), no secrets in logs or responses, RFC 7807 field errors on every write, and the team list paged (default 20, max 50, ordered by name, total returned, index on CompanyId+Name). Scale and cost: desktop mode unchanged; cloud mode adds one primary-key read per person per minute for stamp validation, one indexed CompanyId filter per query, team list bounded to 50 rows per page, sign-in limited by the existing rate limiter plus lockout, no new threads, timers, packages or start-up work beyond one idempotent migration check. The smoke runner costs one process start, about 3 HTTP requests and a temp folder, all cleaned up, and is run on demand only, never at app start. Last-active-Admin rule is enforced in the same UPDATE statement to avoid races. Open items for sign-off: legacy rows without a company go to the oldest company; SshKeyStore is file-based per machine and not company-scoped by this change.
